description: Printed physical naval facilities; uncertain Cape Town type and Philippine port territory remain outside the usable registry.

facilities.notes: Plain blue anchor on white square on Caatinga east coast north of the A45/A47 sea boundary.
White seaplane on green square farther north on Caatinga east coast; physically separate from the port.
Plain white anchor on blue square on Rio de Janeiro coast east of the Pampas land boundary. It does not belong to Pampas.
Blue crane on white square on the southern Buenos Aires city-zone coast. The circular city boundary reaches coast west of the icon, so it is not Patagonia.
Plain white anchor on blue square on the Vancouver Island/western shore; no dockyard ring. Distinct from the white crane farther southeast.
Blue crane on white square at the southeastern British Columbia shore, north of the US border; distinct from the major-port anchor.
Plain white anchor on blue square on southern Nova Scotia, east/north of the A18/A25 boundary origin.
Blue crane on white square farther northeast on the same Nova Scotia coast; separate icon from the port.
Blue plain anchor on white square, east of the Manitoba/Ontario land boundary on Hudson Bay; the rail ends at it.
Separate blue plain anchor on white square on the east side of Hudson Bay/James Bay.
Plain white anchor on blue square on Quebec north shore of the St. Lawrence, east of the Ottawa city circle.
Blue crane on white square on northeastern Quebec shore, west of Labrador; physically distinct from the St. Lawrence port.
Blue crane on white square on northern Chile coastline west of Bolivia, north of the P77/P78 line.
Plain white anchor on blue square on southern western Chile shore, well west of the later P78/A49 boundary; do not duplicate onto A49.
Separate plain blue anchor on white square on northern Colombia east of Panama. No facility symbol on its Pacific coast.
Plain white anchor on blue square on northwestern Cuba shore. It lies north of the A36/A40 line and west of A36/A37 coast junction; A36 only.
Plain blue anchor on white square on northern Ecuador coast, south of Colombia border and north of the P76/P77 division.
Plain blue anchor on white square on French Guiana coast. The symbol is east of the Suriname boundary; Suriname has none.
Plain blue anchor on white square on British Guiana northern coast, east of the Venezuela border.
Plain blue anchor on white square on Iceland southwest coast, northwest of the A3/A4 boundary line. Its square does not bridge the sea boundary; A3 access only.
Plain blue anchor on white square on northern Yucatan shore west of the A36/A40 line. No symbol on the Caribbean or Pacific shore.
Plain blue anchor on white square northeast of the canal symbol on the A40 coast. Canal parallel bars are not another facility; no P76 access icon is printed.
Plain white anchor on blue square on Patagonia east coast south of the Buenos Aires circle. Distinct from the Buenos Aires crane.
Blue crane on white square on northern/central Peru coast, far north of its distinct major port.
Plain white anchor on blue square farther south on Peru coast; the railway starts inland from it.
White seaplane on green square beside Puerto Rico south shore; no anchor port symbol.
Plain white anchor on blue square on Uruguay southern coast, northeast of the A47/A49 boundary starting by Buenos Aires.
Plain blue anchor on white square on the eastern lake shore west of The Northeast land boundary. Retain in Great Lakes; it is not a Northeast facility.
Plain blue anchor on white square on the western Great Lakes water shore; lies in Midwest, west of Great Lakes territory.
Blue crane on white square on New England coast north of the circular New York boundary.
White crane on blue square on the New Orleans city-zone Gulf coast, east of the Mississippi mouth.
White crane on blue square at the New York coast, north of the city-zone boundary ending at the coast/river strip toward Washington.
Blue crane on white square, south of the British Columbia boundary and north of Western US. The inland green airfield is excluded from naval inventory.
White crane on blue square on the San Francisco city-zone coast. A crane is a shipyard, not an anchor port.
White seaplane on green square on west Florida/Gulf shore. Neither a port nor an east-coast A30/A37 facility.
White crane on blue square immediately north of the Mexican border; the P25/P31 sea line meets the coast south of this facility.
White seaplane on green square on Southwest US coast north of its major shipyard; a separate physical icon.
Blue crane on white square on northeastern Texas Gulf coast, west of the New Orleans city boundary.
Plain white anchor on blue square on the western Gulf coast, south of the Texas shipyard.
White seaplane on green square farther south on Texas coast; separate from the major port.
White crane on blue square on Carolinas coast, south of Washington circular border.
White seaplane on green square on northern Carolinas coast; separate from the shipyard.
White crane on blue square on Washington city coast, south of the A25/A30 line. No additional A25 facility access is drawn.
Plain white anchor on blue square on northern Venezuela coast, east of the A40/A41 line ending near Colombia/Venezuela; no facility at A40.

uncertainties.details: The printed board clearly shows a white circled-anchor minor-dockyard symbol, while the supply-path example calls Cape Town a Minor Port. Expected facilities here transcribe the board symbol; reconcile edition/source precedence before applying a different type.

unresolved_facilities.notes: The blue-square plain-anchor major port is definitely in P50. Raster island-group ownership is unresolved between Luzon/Visayas and Mindanao; do not silently assign it to either or count it twice.
